substantive_reconstruction.nonlinear_obstruction: I reconstructed the finite-group discriminator first. Let C2 act on the one-dimensional complex space by the sign character. The action maps are invertible and unitary, and the only complex-linear subspaces are zero and the whole line, so this is a genuine nonzero irreducible representation, not a reducible trivial higher-dimensional action. For f(z)=z^3, oddness gives f(-z)=-f(z), exactly the required functional equation. But f(2)=8 differs from 2f(1), and the distinct cube roots 1 and omega=(-1+i sqrt(3))/2 have the same image. Thus the nonlinear map is neither zero nor a linear isomorphism, even though its zero fiber is {0} and its image is C. Its polynomial is entire. Giving C2 the discrete topology makes the finite group compact and its sign action continuous, so continuity/holomorphicity cannot repair the missing linearity.
substantive_reconstruction.which_steps_fail: The extra h(z)=z^3-z is odd under the same representation, and its zero fiber is {-1,0,1}; this stable subset is not closed under addition, since 1+1=2 is not a zero. Hence one cannot apply irreducibility merely after proving set invariance. The cube already isolates another independent gap: a zero fiber {0} does not imply injectivity without f(v-w)=f(v)-f(w). I also checked the compact U(1) image example. q(z)=z/(1+|z|^2) satisfies q(uz)=u q(z). Its radial range is [0,1/2], since r/(1+r^2)<=1/2 and continuity on r in [0,1] attains that whole interval; all phases occur. The closed nonzero disk is bounded, hence not a complex vector subspace. This map is continuous but explicitly not asserted holomorphic. Neither example relies on an unstated topology for the algebraic theorem.
substantive_reconstruction.linear_kernel_and_image: For the revised conditional theorem, linearity is now an actual question premise over one common field F. If v,w are killed, f(av+bw)=0 for every a,b in F; zero is killed as well. Likewise af(v)+bf(w)=f(av+bw), so the image is a vector subspace. The intertwining equation sends each kernel vector back into the kernel, since the codomain action sends zero to zero; it sends every image vector f(v) to f(phi1(g)v), still in the image. These checks distinguish domain and codomain actions. Stability for g and g inverse supplies equality under each action if desired. No averaging, complement, finite dimension or field-closure theorem is needed to establish these hypotheses of algebraic irreducibility.
substantive_reconstruction.dichotomy_and_inverse: For nonzero f there is a v with f(v) nonzero. The kernel is therefore proper and irreducibility of V1 forces it to be zero; the image is nonzero and irreducibility of V2 forces it to be V2. Now, and only now, equality f(v)=f(w) implies f(v-w)=0 and v=w. Thus the map is bijective. For y=f(v), z=f(w), uniqueness of preimages proves f inverse(ay+bz)=av+bw, giving inverse linearity rather than only a set-theoretic bijection. Applying the original identity to v then gives f inverse(phi2(g)y)=phi1(g)f inverse(y), with the reverse intertwining order correct. This independently supplies the full inverse step omitted by short source shorthand.
substantive_reconstruction.boundaries_grading_and_dependency: The proof applies over any common field and to arbitrary algebraic group representations, including infinite carriers if irreducibility concerns ALL invariant linear subspaces. It does not replace that condition by absence of proper CLOSED subspaces, nor prove a topological inverse. When either carrier is zero, every linear map to or from it is zero; if both are zero that map is also a linear bijection, so the alternatives need not be disjoint. This matches the candidate rather than silently choosing an ordinary nonzero-irrep convention.
